subject: Evaluating Velocity.ai migration: cost reconciliation & package-fit checklist
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Blake <tom@velocity.ai>, Alicia Gomez <alicia@velocity.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluating Velocity.ai migration: cost reconciliation & package-fit checklist

Hi Tom / Alicia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great conversation. As we discussed, to put together a clean migration economics comparison and a proposed Redwood packaging that matches your requirements, could you share a full export of your current usage/pricing for the last 12 months (line items by SKU, committed discounts, overages, and any add-on fees)? The fields that are most helpful on our side are:

- SKU name / description
- Unit price and currency
- Monthly committed units and actual usage
- Any onboarding/one-time professional services fees
- Billing cadence and current termination / notice terms

I've attached a short checklist (redwood-migration-checklist.pdf) that shows how we'll map those line items. If you can drop the spreadsheet here, we'll validate parity and produce a reconciliation that shows: 1) pure unit-cost delta, 2) estimated migration credits / onboarding reduction, and 3) packaging fit (what Redwood bundle maps to your usage).

Suggested next step: 30-minute cost-recon workshop on Wed 6/16 (we can do 10:00 or 15:00 PT) where Connor (SE) will join and walk through the mapping. Let me know what works and please attach the export (or confirm where to pull it from).

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-migration-checklist.pdf (1 page)

From: Tom Blake <tom@velocity.ai>

Subject: Re: Evaluating Velocity.ai migration: cost reconciliation & package-fit checklist

Naomi —

Thanks, attaching the export (velocity_pricing_export.xlsx). A couple quick notes before the workshop:

- The spreadsheet includes three committed contracts across prod, staging, and analytics. The prod contract has a blended discount that isn't shown at the SKU level — procurement can provide a breakdown if you need it.
- We have a currently pending one-time setup fee for our observability integration that may be pushed to Q3; include that in the "one-time" bucket.
- High level ask from our CFO: we need a migration credit that covers at least the first 3 months of production delta for tokens above our committed baseline; open to structuring as credits or a temporary discount.

We can do Wed 6/16 10:00 PT. Connor — can you join to validate model fit?

Tom Blake
Head of Platform Engineering
Velocity.ai
Tom@velocity.ai

Great — appreciate the export. Looping in Marissa (owner for this deal) and Connor (SE) to own the mapping plus the workshop. Connor: for the 10:00 PT slot on Wed I suggest we focus the session on:

1) Confirming which SKUs map to Redwood product lines (in particular the real-time inference vs batch embed SKU split).
2) Validating the blended discount and how to model it (we may need a procurement-level breakdown).
3) Proposing a 3-month migration credit structure and preferred billing mechanics (credit vs temporary discount).

I'll kick off the internal reconciliation after the workshop and share a one-page reconciliation with three scenarios: conservative, expected, and aggressive (showing per-token delta and estimated op-ex savings from batching + KV caching).

Naomi

Attachments: redwood-migration-checklist.pdf (1 page)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Blake <tom@velocity.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Evaluating Velocity.ai migration: cost reconciliation & package-fit checklist

Tom / Naomi —

Thanks for the export and the context. We ran a quick first-pass model and here are the headline proposals to discuss at 10:00 PT:

- Packaging: Recommend Redwood "Dedicated Plus" for prod (predictable throughput) + "Hosted" for analytics. This reduces your per-token bill by ~18% on expected 6-month consumption vs your blended current.
- Migration credit: Offer a 3-month credit that phases: 60% month 1, 30% month 2, 10% month 3, applied to overage/production tokens above committed baseline. Can be structured as a usage credit on month-end invoice or a one-time bill adjustment (your preference).
- One-time onboarding: We can absorb up to 50% of your observability integration fee if committed to a 12-month Dedicated contract.
- Contract mechanics: Standard SOW + 90 days notice termination for Dedicated. We can shorten to 60 days with a modest premium if Velocity needs more flexibility.

Attached: proposed-counteroffer-summary.xlsx — includes a scenario table (conservative/expected/aggressive) and an estimated run-rate bridge. At the workshop Connor will walk the technical assumptions (batching assumptions, KV cache hit rates). Karthik will be available for commercial/legal tradeoffs if needed.

Action items for workshop: please confirm whether procurement can provide the blended-discount breakout (if not, we'll model with scenarios). Also confirm preferred credit type (invoice credit vs end-of-term bill adjustment).

Thanks — talk at 10am.

Marissa Cole
Principal Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: proposed-counteroffer-summary.xlsx (Excel, 1 file)

From: Tom Blake <tom@velocity.ai>

Marissa / Naomi —

Appreciate the clear proposal. The phased 3-month credit looks reasonable — procurement prefers invoice credits (easier for our month-to-month tracking). Procurement will provide the blended-discount breakout by EOD Friday.

Next steps from our side: procurement will issue a PO once we have the final commercial language; legal will want the 90-day vs 60-day option spelled out. Can you send a draft exhibit that includes the credit schedule and the onboarding absorption clause?

I'll loop Alicia (cc'd) who will own the PO / procurement coordination.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop notes.

Tom
